resource_verdicts.PCIe: Host/device copy commands run near prior matched-stack bulk-copy throughput; in the long attention envelope ALL copy union is9.11% and overlap about8microseconds. Transfer matters but this capture does not support PCIe-only dominance. This is an envelope, not full-prefill critical path or physical wire counters.
resource_verdicts.GPU_compute: Compute-command coverage77.31% of long attention envelope, QSA60launch service33.963s. This identifies device compute commands as priority but DOES NOT determine ALU/XMX saturation versus VRAM/cache/SLM/barrier/dependency limits inside kernels.
resource_verdicts.CPU: Main thread98.420CPU s includes69.696CPU s in explicit GPU waits and28.723CPU s outside waits. Host grouping0.106CPU s; GEMM submission123192calls5.643CPU s; upload submission5.753CPU s; source copy4.846CPU s; unclassified12.329CPU s. Polling alone is not CPU latency evidence; launch/packing and gap causality remain candidates.
resource_verdicts.RAM: Host source-copy CPU time measured, physical RAM traffic/bandwidth not measured in this run. Historical36.87GB/s six-core streaming read is operation/stack scoped reference, not current utilization or random-access capacity.
resource_verdicts.VRAM: Whole-command D2D requested payload76.948GB; payload/service about163GB/s (logical read+write about326GB/s). Copy throughput is not kernel DRAM traffic. No per-kernel cache/VRAM bandwidth or occupancy collected.
resource_verdicts.scheduling: Copies and compute almost entirely serialize in the observed safe route. Overlap or fewer host launches may remove exposed time, but9%copy coverage cannot alone establish a600/1000tok/s path. Gaps12.893s of long attention envelope are uncovered commands, not proved hardware idle or CPU causality.
